newsitem.title: USA: Clinton returns to putting green, praises Packers.
newsitem.headline: Clinton returns to putting green, praises Packers.

text.p: President Bill Clinton enjoyed two of the presidency's perquisites on Tuesday, putting on his private golf green for the first time since his March knee injury and then posing with the Super Bowl champion Green Bay Packers.

Under a sunny, blue sky, Clinton returned to his beloved pastime of golf for the first time since March 14, the night he tore a tendon in his right knee, which forced him to have emergency surgery and kept him on crutches for two months.

The president, who has been walking with a cane since last week, took to the private green on the White House South Lawn Tuesday afternoon after his doctors approved his returning to the art of putting.
He is not expected to resume full-blown golfing until the end of the summer at the earliest.

After returning briefly to the White House, Clinton then strolled to another part of the lawn to congratulate the Green Bay Packers, who in January beat the New England Patriots 35-21 to win Super Bowl XXXI.
The victory in the football championship was the first for the Wisconsin team since it won the first two Super Bowls in 1967 and 1968.
Clinton congratulated the about two dozen team members who came to the White House and accepted a green, gold and white Packers football jacket and a game ball from them as mememtos.

"I got a lot of good advice, when we were up in the White House having our pictures taken, from the players about my knee therapy, and I appreciate that," he said. "What I need is some advice about how to make sure it never happens again."
He also praised the unusually close relationship between the Packers and the Green Bay community, which owns the team and has kept it in the midwestern city.
"In a world where ... people move from team to team and teams move from town to town, the Green Bay Packers are something special, unique, old fashioned and heart-warming," Clinton said.

"It really means something to the rest of the country to see the relationship between Green Bay and the Packers and to know that, come what may, it will be there next year, and the year after that," Clinton added.

Mike Holmgren, the team's coach, reminded the Packers that it would be tough to win a second straight Super Bowl and then joked: "This is pretty nice ... I'd like to come back here again this time next year."
